pairs.question: Quem mittam et quis ibit nobis?
pairs.derivation: Dropped speech-frame 'et audivi vocem Domini dicentis' before the question and 'et dixi' before the answer. The Lord asks whom to send; Isaiah answers 'here I am, send me.' Answer is the whole reply (one clause).

pairs.question: Custos quid de nocte? Custos quid de nocte?
pairs.answer: Venit mane et nox si quaeritis quaerite convertimini venite.
pairs.derivation: Question is the call from Seir to the watchman (verse 11, after the frame 'ad me clamat ex Seir'); dropped the speech-tag 'dixit custos' before the watchman's reply (verse 12). The watchman genuinely answers the 'what of the night?' query.

pairs.question: Quid dixerunt viri isti et unde venerunt ad te?
pairs.answer: De terra longinqua venerunt ad me de Babylone.
pairs.derivation: Dropped narrative frame 'introiit autem Isaias propheta ad regem Ezechiam et dixit ei' before the question and 'et dixit Ezechias' before the answer. Hezekiah's reply answers the 'unde venerunt' part directly; it is the whole reply, so no trimming needed.

pairs.question: Quid viderunt in domo tua?
pairs.answer: Omnia quae in domo mea sunt viderunt non fuit res quam non ostenderim eis in thesauris meis.
pairs.derivation: Dropped speech-tag 'et dixit' before the question and 'et dixit Ezechias' before the answer. Isaiah asks what they saw; Hezekiah answers directly. Answer is the entire reply.

pairs.question: Quis est iste qui venit de Edom tinctis vestibus de Bosra iste formonsus in stola sua gradiens in multitudine fortitudinis suae?
pairs.answer: Ego qui loquor iustitiam et propugnator sum ad salvandum.
pairs.derivation: Question is the questioner's whole utterance (the description 'iste formonsus...fortitudinis suae' is part of the question); the answer begins at 'ego qui loquor iustitiam', which is the figure's self-identifying reply. Cut at the verse end; verse 2 opens a new question.

pairs.question: Quare ergo rubrum est indumentum tuum et vestimenta tua sicut calcantium in torculari?
pairs.answer: Torcular calcavi solus et de gentibus non est vir mecum.
pairs.derivation: Verse 2 is the follow-up question; the answer is the operative first sentence of verse 3 ('torcular calcavi solus et de gentibus non est vir mecum'), which directly answers why his garment is red. Cut before 'calcavi eos in furore meo...', which elaborates rather than answers.
